messages.content: I need to know the current time on my machine, using the command echo %time%

function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a given command using the os.system() function specifically for Windows operating systems. For multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For complex tasks, create and run a .bat file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The Windows command line instruction(s) to be executed. Use '&&' between commands for multiple instructions. For complex sequences, encapsulate the logic within a .bat file and provide the execution command here.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to execute "echo %time%" on their machine (Windows). We have tool to execute OS commands via cmd_controller_execute. So we should call it.

We will use the function. Provide JSON input with command field set to "cmd /c echo %time%". Or just "echo %time%".

But note that environment variable expansion occurs only when running inside CMD shell; if you pass directly to system maybe not expanded? Usually os.system runs through cmd.exe - but I'm not sure. In python's os.system, passing "echo %time%" might work because it's passed to cmd.exe which expands variables. But safer to prefix with "cmd /C" or "call"? Let's do "cmd /C echo %%time%%"? Wait double percent needed when used from batch script. From interactive command prompt, single percent works. When calling from program, I think single percent also works. We'll try simple "echo %time%".

Thus produce function call.
